data.name: Stephen
data.gender_notes: Stephen is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek 'Stepheos' and the Hebrew 'Stephanos', meaning 'crown, wreath'. In the Bible, Stephen was a deacon and a martyr. In Christianity, he is regarded as the first Christian martyr. The name Stephen carries the meaning “Crown, wreath” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Stephen usually hope their child will grow to embody crown, wreath and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes spiritual crown or reward for a devoted and faithful life.
data.etymology: Stephen belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Crown, wreath.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Stephen total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: סטיבן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם סטיבן מקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו כתר או עטרה, ומתייחס לכתר הנצחי שמוענק לנוצרים המאמינים. השם נגזר מהמילה היוונית סטפאנוס, שפירושה כתר.

in_greek.name: Στεφανός
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Στεφανός είναι όνομα ελληνικής προέλευσης και σημαίνει το κατ'εξοχήν στεφάνι ή το στεφάνι του θριάμβου. Το όνομα αναφέρεται στο στέφανο που φοριόταν ως σύμβολο νίκης ή τιμής στην αρχαία Ελλάδα.

in_latin.name: Stephanus
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Stephanus is derived from the Greek word Stephanos, meaning crown or wreath. In Christian tradition, it symbolizes the crown of martyrdom and spiritual victory.

in_english.name: Stephen
in_english.meaning: crown or wreath, symbolizing spiritual victory
in_english.long_meaning: The name Stephen originates from the Greek word Στεφανός (Stephanos), meaning crown or wreath. In Christian tradition, Stephen was one of the first deacons and the first Christian martyr, making the name significant in Christian heritage. It symbolizes spiritual victory and the crown of martyrdom.

data.cultural_impact: Stephen holds significant cultural impact in Christianity as the first recorded martyr in the history of the faith. His story of unwavering faith and commitment to the teachings of Jesus, even in the face of violent persecution, has been a source of inspiration and transformation in the lives of countless Christians throughout history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Stephen holds deep spiritual significance in Christianity, as it is symbolic of the ultimate reward for those who remain steadfast in their faith – a crown or wreath of victory in the eternal kingdom of God. The story of Stephen serves as a reminder that genuine commitment to our beliefs and the message of love and compassion that Jesus brought to the world, may come with a price, but the eternal reward is worth the sacrifice.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Stephen, meaning "crown" in Greek, symbolizes the reward of martyrdom and faithfulness in Christ. In the New Testament, Saint Stephen is the first Christian martyr, who wore a crown of martyrdom through his sacrifice and unwavering faith.

biblical_reference.note: Stephen was one of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles and the first Christian martyr.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Stephen, a deacon in the early Christian church, was the first martyr of the faith. The name Stephen carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Stephen remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Peter Stephen in Dublin, Ireland credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Stephen, which means "Crown, wreath". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
